card.architecture: Ideogram 4 — conditional UNET with a frozen first-step residual correction, separate unconditional UNET, DualModelGuider + CFGOverride + Ideogram4Scheduler, Qwen3-VL 8B encoder, Flux2 VAE; fp8 (no bf16 published)
card.summary: Ideogram's open text-to-image model, renowned for best-in-class typography/text rendering and prompt adherence. Uses a two-UNet guidance scheme (both ~9.3 GB models resident at once), so it's VRAM-heavy — tight on a 24 GB card. A reversible conditional-model correction reduces the repeatable unwanted card/text composition so ordinary prompts can be used directly.
use_cases: legible in-image text, logos, posters, typography
strong prompt adherence and layout control
card.commercial_use: open weights — verify the Ideogram 4 license for your use
card.pick_when: You need accurate in-image text / typography or top prompt adherence and have a 24 GB card to spare.

prompt.guidance: Descriptive natural language; quote literal text to render it. Structured JSON captions are also supported for fine layout control.
prompt.example: A retro travel poster, bold headline reading "IDEOGRAM" in cream serif letters over a sunset mountain range, clean vector style
prompt.instructions: Write descriptive natural language; to render literal text wrap the exact string in double quotes and keep it short. Defaults: 20 steps, base CFG 7 with a late-step CFG of 3 over the last 30%, euler, Ideogram4 schedule (mu 0.5, std 1.75). Native ~1K. No user negative prompt (an unconditional model handles guidance).
dont: Expect a separate negative prompt to apply
Run other big models at the same time (VRAM is tight)
prompt.negative_guidance: No user negative prompt — guidance comes from the dedicated unconditional UNet.

negative.note: Guidance uses a dedicated unconditional model; no user negative.

speed.note: Two ~9.3 GB fp8 UNets resident during sampling; VRAM-tight on 24 GB.
speed.measured_note: Not yet benchmarked on this box.

ui_help.note: Describe what you want in plain words; quote any text you want spelled out. Best here for readable text and posters.
